key_insight: Egocentric human video can be a better large-scale pretraining source than real-robot trajectories for embodied AI, despite lacking direct robot action labels. The paper shows that human video can outperform costly teleoperated robot data when used thoughtfully for embodied pretraining.
problem_solved: Embodied foundation models need massive amounts of diverse training data, but real-robot teleoperation is expensive, slow to collect, and limited in behavioral/environmental diversity. This paper addresses the data bottleneck in embodied pretraining by exploring a scalable alternative: egocentric human video.
method: Compare egocentric human video against teleoperated real-robot trajectories as pretraining sources for embodied models.
Leverage human first-person video to provide scalable, diverse visual experience for learning embodiment-relevant representations.
Evaluate whether data scale and diversity can compensate for weaker action supervision compared with robot trajectories.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests that cheaper and more abundant human video may be a powerful substitute or complement to robot-collected data in embodied pretraining. It opens a practical path to scaling embodied AI without relying exclusively on expensive robot data collection.
